MEMORANDUM

  Agenda Item #: 4 _
  Meeting Date: June 9, 2020

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL

THRU:  KENNETH RUKAVINA, ACTING CITY MANAGER

FROM:  CARL MORITZ, URBAN FORESTER

SUBJECT: CONSIDERATION OF PARKLANDS COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATIONS OF
  MAY 14, 2020

DATE:  JUNE 9, 2020

Issue/Purpose

The purpose of this memorandum is to transmit Committee recommendations from the Parklands
Committee May 14, 2020 meeting for the City Council’s approval.

Background/Discussion

At its meeting of May 14, 2020, the Parklands Committee reviewed three applications. The first item was
a citizen application for Tree Removal; the Committee’s recommendation for this item has been appealed
and the appeal hearing is scheduled for June 23rd. The second item was a citizen application for Tree
Removal and Change of Designation reported below. The third item was a citizen application for Change
to Parklands to landscape a portion of the bluffs adjacent to Lunada Bay Elementary School, which is
reported in a separate staff report.

PC Item 2.  PC-535-20; Application for Change of Designation and removal of one Peruvian pepper
  tree located in the parkway adjacent to 3900 Via Palomino

  Applicant:  Allan Rigg
  6415 Via Canada
  Rancho Palos Verdes, CA 90275

This application was introduced by staff as a request to remove one Peruvian pepper tree and replace it
with another Peruvian pepper in a better location. Staff indicated the pepper requested for removal was

  1
 miss-shaped and badly located below a She-Oak. The previous designated street tree for Via Palomino.
The new owners of the home requested approval to remove the badly located and misshaped pepper to
frame the driveway with a matching pepper. The Forester indicated the Camphor tree was designated for
the street tree in 2001 but none have been planted and only a few exist in the neighborhood and none on
the street. Peruvian peppers were more in character than the camphor and the She-Oak was no longer the
designated street tree.

The applicant provided a PowerPoint presentation and reiterated the reasons for the request were to
improve the unique feeling of the neighborhood and improve fire safety. The removal would not affect
screening or privacy and the applicant indicated the neighborhood character would be enhanced by the
addition of a Peruvian pepper that was located appropriately.

The Committee all agreed the pepper could be removed and the new pepper planted as the street tree in
this location. One member indicated the designated street tree should be re-considered since none have
been planted but had no issue with allowing a pepper to be planted.

Action: Committee Member Groves motioned, seconded by Cooper, to recommend to the City Council
approval to remove one Peruvian pepper tree and Change of designation to plant one Peruvian pepper as
the designated street tree adjacent to 3900 Via Palomino. A $500 payment to the Tree Bank and removal
of the stump are required. The vote was (4-0, in favor, Richie-Bray recused).

Notification

Interested parties attending the Parklands Committee meeting were made aware that the above noted
recommendations would be transmitted to the City Council. This item is also noticed in the standard
manner for City Council meetings.

Recommendation

It is recommended that the City Council review and approve the Parklands Committee recommended
actions PC-535-20.
